effects.log: You burn it. The applicant leaves with the empty box. The board never meets again, and {npc} never mentions it, which is how you know.

events.text: With so many spouses the year has grown crowded: birthdays, wedding days, the days each of them first came through the gate. Last month you forgot one. You are not sure whose. {npc} unrolls a calendar three feet long, written in five colours of ink.

choices.text: Learn every date by heart

effects.log: You study the calendar like a sword manual and dream in dates. {npc} tests you at breakfast.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to remind you

effects.log: A sigh with years in it. From then on a little red slip appears by your bowl on every important morning.

choices.text: Declare one feast day for everyone

effects.log: One shared day is fair, and also, the house agrees, a little lazy. They hold the shared feast and keep their own days too.

events.text: Disaster: two wedding days fall on the same date this year, and two members of the household have each planned a surprise outing for you. One is a boat on the lake at dawn. One is a mountain shrine at dawn. The lake and the mountain are a morning's ride apart.

choices.text: Attempt both at full speed

ok.log: You reach the boat at dawn and the shrine at a late dawn of its own. It becomes a famous morning.

fail.log: You reach the shrine soaked from the lake and two hours late. Both outings end at the same inn, sulking together.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to arbitrate

effects.log: {npc} moves the boat to the evening, with lanterns. Nobody can say why they did not think of it.

choices.text: Combine them: a shrine reached by boat

effects.log: There is a shrine on an island. Both surprises become one long day. Somebody is seasick.

events.text: On a morning that is on no calendar at all, the whole household is waiting in the hall with one cake. {npc} explains: they have made a day for the house itself, the day the second spouse came through the gate and a couple became a household.

choices.text: Write the day onto the calendar

effects.log: You write it in gold ink at the very top. {npc} pretends it is not the best day of {his} year.

choices.text: Raise a toast to the house

effects.log: Your toast is short, for once. Everyone notices. Several people weep into the cake.

choices.text: Ask whose idea it was

effects.log: Everyone points at {npc}. {npc} points at the newest member of the household. Nobody will take the credit, which is the point.

events.text: The household has been quarrelling for a season. {npc} comes to your study at midnight with an inkstone and a sheet of fine paper. "Great sects end their wars with treaties," {he} says. "We are a great sect of bad tempers. Help me draft one."
events.arc: The Treaty of the Plum Tree

choices.text: Draft it together through the night

effects.log: By dawn there are twelve articles and a preamble. Article nine is about the bathhouse. It is the most important article.

choices.text: Say treaties are for enemies

effects.log: "So are we, lately," says {npc}, and drafts it alone. A copy is on your pillow in the morning.

choices.text: Add one article: nobody sleeps angry

effects.log: {npc} writes it as article one, looks at it, and says it will never work. You both sign it anyway.

events.text: The treaty is read aloud in the hall before the whole household. The newest member asks for an amendment about the cat. Another wants the bathhouse article struck out. {npc} sits with a brush, waiting to see whether you will defend the text.
events.arc: The Treaty of the Plum Tree

choices.text: Defend every article

ok.log: You defend article nine with such passion that the hall bursts out laughing, and signs.

fail.log: You defend article nine for an hour. The hall signs only to make you stop. It still counts.

choices.text: Accept the amendments

effects.log: The cat gets an article of its own. The treaty is longer now, and loved. Everyone signs.

choices.text: Put it to a vote

effects.log: They vote. Article nine passes by one voice. Nobody will say whose.

events.text: The treaty hangs in the hall. It is broken almost at once, article three, and the one who broke it is you: you shouted at the steward over a lost key. The household watches to see whether the head of the house is above the law.
events.arc: The Treaty of the Plum Tree

choices.text: Pay the treaty's penalty in public

effects.log: The penalty is washing every dish in the house for a week. You do it. Nobody breaks the treaty again for a year.

choices.text: Argue that the steward started it

effects.log: Technically true. Nobody cares. {npc} adds article thirteen, on the subject of technically true.

choices.text: Apologise to the steward first

effects.log: The steward is so astonished that the quarrel in the house simply ends, as if it had forgotten what it was for.

events.text: A famous scholar from the capital has heard that your household of several spouses lives in real harmony, and wants to write a book about how it is done. {npc} is flattered and suspicious in equal parts. The scholar has already started taking notes on your doorstep.

choices.text: Let the scholar stay a month

effects.log: The scholar eats with you, asks questions over every meal, and writes in a small book with a very sharp brush.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to decide

effects.log: {npc} interviews the scholar for an hour and allows a fortnight. The scholar comes out looking shaken.

choices.text: Send the scholar away

effects.log: The scholar writes the book anyway, about another family, and gets everything wrong. You read it aloud at dinner.

events.text: The book is out: The Harmonious House, in three volumes. It calls {npc} "stern but just", the newest member of the household "a charming sprite", and you "the central pillar", which everyone finds very funny. Suddenly the whole house is self-conscious about everything.

choices.text: Read the worst passages aloud at dinner

effects.log: You read them in a scholar's voice. By the end the whole table is weeping with laughter.

choices.text: Write to the scholar with corrections

effects.log: The scholar promises a corrected edition. The house argues for a month about what the corrections should say.

choices.text: Be the central pillar for a week

effects.log: You stand very straight and speak in maxims. {npc} asks the steward, privately, whether you are ill.

events.text: Readers of the book have begun arriving at your gate to see the Harmonious House in person. Today there are eleven of them, with copies to sign. Inside, two members of the household are in the middle of their first proper shouting match in years, about the shape of a teapot.

choices.text: Invite the readers in to see it

effects.log: The readers watch the teapot quarrel wide-eyed. It ends in laughter, as quarrels here do. They go home with a truer book.

choices.text: Sign their books at the gate, slowly

ok.log: You sign eleven books with long dedications. By the last one the teapot question is settled.

fail.log: A reader hears a teapot hit a wall. The second edition has a new chapter.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to go out to them

effects.log: {npc} goes to the gate, every inch stern but just, and sends the readers home with pears. {He} enjoys it more than {he} admits.

events.text: A great house of the capital, whose own household is in chaos, has written to offer {npc} the post of steward of its estate: a hundred servants, a salary in gold, a carriage. It is the highest compliment one house can pay another. {npc} has left the letter on your desk, open.
events.arc: The Offer from the Great House

choices.text: Ask {npc} what {he} wants

effects.log: {npc} looks at you a long time. "Nobody has ever asked me that," {he} says. "Let me think."

choices.text: Make a counter-offer (20 taels)

mem.note: tried to pay me to stay

effects.log: {npc} accepts the silver gravely and gives it to the kitchen. It is the wrong kind of answer, but an answer.

choices.text: Refuse the great house yourself

effects.log: You write the refusal in your own hand. {npc} learns of it from the great house's reply. It is a quiet month.

events.text: The household has heard. The newest member, who has never once agreed with {npc} about anything, has written a petition begging {him} to stay and got every servant to sign it. It is pinned to {his} door. {npc} pretends not to have read it eleven times.
events.arc: The Offer from the Great House

choices.text: Sign it too

effects.log: Your name goes at the bottom, smaller than the cook's. {npc} notices the size and the place, and approves.

choices.text: Take it down, for {his} dignity

effects.log: {npc} asks where it went, a little too quickly. You give it back.

choices.text: Write a counter-petition as a joke

ok.log: Yours demands that {npc} leave at once so you may finally win an argument. {npc} laughs so hard {he} has to sit down.

fail.log: Half the servants miss the joke and are very upset with you.

events.text: {npc} has decided. {He} will go to the capital for one season, set the great house in order, and come home. "They need me," {he} says. "You only want me. Both are good. One is more interesting."
events.arc: The Offer from the Great House

choices.text: Let {npc} go, proudly

effects.log: {npc} sets the great house in order in four months. A plaque thanking your household for the loan hangs above the carp pond.

choices.text: Go with {npc} for the season

effects.log: You spend a season carrying ledgers behind the new steward. At home the house runs without you both, slightly worse, happily.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stay after all

effects.log: {npc} stays. {He} keeps the letter in a drawer and takes it out sometimes, to read the compliment.

events.text: You come into the hall to find the whole household arguing about your funeral. Nobody is ill. It is simply a matter of planning, {npc} explains: who walks first, who carries the tablet, who gives the eulogy. You are very welcome to sit in.

choices.text: Sit in, and take notes

effects.log: The debate is fierce. You learn that three people want to give the eulogy and two have already written one.

choices.text: Announce that you will live forever

effects.log: "Of course," says {npc}, "but just in case." The meeting goes on. You are given a cushion.

choices.text: Leave the room, appalled

effects.log: Through the door behind you, you hear {npc} say: "Item two. The music."

events.text: To settle it, you write your own instructions, in your own hand, and seal them. All that week the members of the household come to your study, one at a time, with tea, to make a quiet suggestion.

choices.text: Give every one of them a part

effects.log: Everyone gets a part. The order of the procession is a masterpiece of diplomacy. You are rather proud of it.

choices.text: Give {npc} the eulogy

effects.log: The others accept it, because it is {npc}. But each of them, separately, slips a note into the eulogy.

choices.text: Write only: have a good feast

effects.log: One line, sealed. When the house finds out it is furious, and then agrees it is the best idea anyone has had.

events.text: Years go by, and the sealed instructions sit in the little box nobody may open. One evening {npc} reads you the eulogy {he} wrote, all of it, while you are still here to hear it, because otherwise, {he} says, it seemed a waste.

choices.text: Listen to the end

effects.log: It is funny and true, and a little unkind in the right places. Afterwards neither of you can speak for a while.

choices.text: Correct the facts

effects.log: {npc} corrects your correction. You are both right, about different leaking roofs.

choices.text: Write one for {npc} in return

ok.log: Yours is shorter and worse. {npc} keeps it folded in {his} sleeve from then on.

fail.log: You cannot finish it. {npc} says the unfinished one is better.

events.text: The whole household is going to the Temple of Nine Bells to burn incense for the house. There are two carriages, one cart, one mule with opinions, and a household with firm views on who rides with whom. {npc} has drawn up a seating plan. It is in its third draft.

choices.text: Use {npc}'s third draft

effects.log: "A record," says {npc}, when the third draft survives a whole morning.

choices.text: Ride the mule yourself

effects.log: You ride the mule. It is a terrible decision. Both carriages are united in watching you suffer.

choices.text: Walk, and let them sort it out

effects.log: You walk beside the carriages. Every half hour somebody leans out to report on the quarrel inside.

events.text: On the second day, in a pine pass, a band of mountain bandits steps onto the road. Their leader, a cheerful giant, asks for your silver. Before you can draw, the whole household has climbed out of the carriages and is standing behind you with umbrellas, a teapot and the mule.

choices.text: Fight, with the house at your back

ok.log: You knock down the giant. The house knocks down the rest with umbrellas. The mule takes one bandit personally.

fail.log: The giant knocks you flat. The household knocks the giant flat. You will be reminded of this for years.

choices.text: Pay them to go away (20 taels)

effects.log: {npc} haggles the bandits down on principle. They take the silver and recommend a very good inn.

choices.text: Let {npc} talk to them

mem.note: let me talk to the bandits

effects.log: {npc} speaks to the giant for one minute about honest work. The bandits escort you to the temple and carry the luggage.

events.text: At the temple the household burns incense together, one stick each, in one bronze burner. A monk asks what the household prays for. {npc}, who is never at a loss, has no answer, and looks at you.

choices.text: Pray for the house to stay as it is

effects.log: One wish, many sticks. The smoke rises straight up, which the monk says is a very good sign and is probably the weather.

choices.text: Pray aloud for {npc}

effects.log: The others hear you say the name. Nobody minds as much as you feared, and {npc} does not mind at all.

choices.text: Give the temple a bell (10 taels)

effects.log: The monks hang a bell with your household's name on it. It rings slightly out of tune, like a household. You love it.

events.text: A matchmaker arrives at your gate with a portfolio, having heard that your house takes spouses. Before you reach the gate, {npc} has seated the matchmaker in the front hall, served the cheapest tea in the house, and begun asking about the candidates' debts.
events.arc: The Matchmaker Calls on a Full House

choices.text: Let {npc} interview the matchmaker

effects.log: {npc} conducts the interview like a magistrate. The matchmaker leaves sweating and recommends your house to nobody.

choices.text: Look at the portfolio yourself

effects.log: You glance at one portrait. The whole house knows by dinner. The soup is very thin.

choices.text: Ask the matchmaker for a gift for {npc}

effects.log: The confused matchmaker recommends a jade seller. {npc} is not fooled for a moment, and is delighted anyway.

events.text: The matchmaker is back, and not for you. The newest member of the household has a cousin of marrying age who wants a match in a house as well run as yours. The matchmaker would like {npc} to advise, and offers a fee.
events.arc: The Matchmaker Calls on a Full House

choices.text: Encourage {npc} to take the fee

effects.log: {npc} advises at length. The cousin is matched within a season. The fee buys a new lantern for the gate.

choices.text: Offer your own advice as well

effects.log: The matchmaker writes your advice down out of politeness, then crosses it out in front of you.

choices.text: Suggest {npc} become a matchmaker

effects.log: {npc} considers it seriously for a week, then matches the gatekeeper and the cook as a trial. It works.

events.text: Quietly, {npc} has become the most sought-after match adviser in the district. Matchmakers queue at your gate with portfolios for {his} opinion. Your house has become a matchmaking hall, and the hall tea is no longer the cheapest in the house.
events.arc: The Matchmaker Calls on a Full House

choices.text: Charge a fee at the gate

effects.log: {npc} doubles your modest fee the next day without telling you. The queue does not get any shorter.

choices.text: Keep the gate free

effects.log: The house's name spreads as a house of good counsel. Your own reputation rises entirely on {npc}'s back.

choices.text: Ask how {npc} would have judged you

effects.log: "I would have sent you back to the matchmaker twice," says {npc}. Then, more gently: "The third time, yes."

events.text: {npc}, matchmaker of the river district, has a red fan, a portfolio and a reputation: three hundred weddings, two divorces, one lawsuit. {He} sits down in your best chair without being asked. "Three candidates," {he} says. "Choose one, or I choose for you."

choices.text: Hear the three

effects.log: {npc} snaps the fan shut. "Good. They come to tea next month, all three, on the same afternoon. It saves time."

choices.text: Ask about the fee first

effects.log: "Ten taels if it ends in a wedding," says {npc}, "and a goose either way." You decide not to ask about the goose.

choices.text: Refuse, politely

effects.log: {npc} writes your name in a small black book. "Next year," {he} says, and leaves the fan behind as a promise.

events.text: Tea. The first candidate, a scholar, faints at the sight of your sword. The second, a sect disciple, talks for an hour about meridians and asks to take your pulse. The third, a merchant's heir, brought an abacus and has priced your house. {npc} sits in the corner, beaming, eating all the cakes.

choices.text: Revive the scholar with tea

effects.log: The scholar wakes, apologises, and faints again at the second sword. You become friends, carefully, without swords.

choices.text: Let the disciple take your pulse

effects.log: The diagnosis is accurate and deeply unromantic. You learn something about your liver.

choices.text: Ask the heir what your house is worth

effects.log: Less than you hoped. The heir offers to improve it, for a fee. You are almost tempted.

events.text: {npc} comes for your verdict and is not surprised that it is none of the three. "Nobody chooses the first three," {he} says. "They are there so you know what you do not want." The red fan points at the young server who poured the tea all afternoon and laughed in the right places.

choices.text: Ask the server's name

effects.log: {npc} smiles behind the fan. "My godchild. The name is theirs to tell. Come to tea again next month. Alone."

choices.text: Accuse {npc} of planning this

effects.log: "Of course I planned it," says {npc}. "Three hundred weddings. Did you think they happen by chance?"

choices.text: Ask for three new candidates

effects.log: {npc} sighs and opens the portfolio again. The server is not in it.

events.text: The server from the teahouse, {npc}, is waiting at the same table, alone this time, with a pot of tea and a list of honest questions written on a fan. The first question is: "Did you really not know it was a trap?"

choices.text: "I knew by the second cake."

effects.log: {npc} laughs. The rest of the questions go faster after that, and so does the afternoon.

choices.text: Answer every question honestly

effects.log: {npc} writes your answers on the back of the fan. It is the most honest afternoon you have had in years.

choices.text: Flee before the first question

effects.log: {npc} keeps the fan, unanswered, which is worse than any answer.

events.text: A year of teas. {npc}'s fan of questions is full on both sides now. The old matchmaker has stopped pretending not to arrange your meetings, and has started measuring doorways.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to marry you

effects.log: "Finally," says {npc}. The old matchmaker, listening at the window, bursts in with a goose. Three hundred and one.

choices.text: Keep it a friendship

effects.log: {npc} agrees, a little sadly, and stays a friend. The matchmaker refuses to speak to you for a month.

choices.text: Write question forty on the fan

effects.log: Your question is about the future. {npc} takes the fan home to think. Some answers want time.

events.text: Your first proper meeting with {npc}, arranged by the matchmaker, is on a pleasure boat on the lotus lake. Halfway across, you both stand up to point at the same heron, and the boat turns over. You are now standing waist-deep in a lotus pond in your best clothes, holding your teacups.

choices.text: Finish your tea anyway

mem.note: finished the tea in the pond

effects.log: {npc} stares at you, then sips {his} own tea, which is now mostly pond. The boatman applauds.

choices.text: Carry {npc} to the bank

mem.note: carried me out of the pond

ok.log: You carry {npc} to the bank with great dignity. The dignity lasts until the mud.

fail.log: {npc} laughs so hard the herons leave. You both fell over again.

choices.text: Blame the heron

effects.log: "Clearly the heron," agrees {npc}. Together you write a stern letter of complaint to nobody.

events.text: The second meeting, a quiet walk in the plum orchard, is ended by bees. The third, at an elegant restaurant, ends when the kitchen catches fire. The matchmaker, wringing both hands, suggests that perhaps Heaven is against it. {npc} suggests a fourth meeting.

choices.text: Agree to a fourth at once

effects.log: Fourth meeting: a tea shop. Nothing happens at all. You are both strangely disappointed.

choices.text: Choose somewhere disaster-proof

ok.log: A bare stone courtyard. A pigeon finds you there. You agree it counts as a success.

fail.log: The stone courtyard has one loose stone. You twist an ankle. {npc} carries you, this time.

choices.text: Buy a temple luck charm (3 taels)

effects.log: The charm works for exactly one afternoon of perfect peace, which you both find boring.

events.text: {npc} turns up at your gate with a list: Lotus Lake. Plum Orchard. The Kitchen Fire. The Pigeon. "Our history," {he} says. "I would like to add to it. Possibly for a very long time." The matchmaker is hiding behind a cart, mouthing the word yes.

choices.text: Say yes, and propose properly

effects.log: You propose under the gate. A roof tile falls and misses you both by a finger. {npc} adds it to the list. The wedding is in spring.

choices.text: Ask for one ordinary meeting first

effects.log: One ordinary afternoon. Nothing burns and nothing floods. You agree it was a little sad, and keep meeting anyway.

choices.text: Say Heaven might be right

effects.log: {npc} folds the list very carefully and goes. The pigeon, oddly, keeps visiting you.

events.text: {npc}, the most famous matchmaker in three counties, has decided that you are {his} final great work. You have said no four times. {He} has taken this as the opening of negotiations.
events.arc: The Matchmaker Who Will Not Give Up

choices.text: Say no a fifth time

effects.log: {npc} writes "five" in a small book, very pleased, and leaves a list of candidates on your table anyway.

choices.text: Hide whenever {npc} comes

effects.log: You learn every back door in the district. {npc} learns them faster.

choices.text: Agree to one meeting, to end it

effects.log: "Wise," says {npc}, bowing, and does not leave for three hours.

events.text: {npc} appears at your training ground with a candidate, then at the bathhouse with a candidate's portrait, then on the roof of your inn at midnight, slightly out of breath, with a candidate's horoscope. "You climb walls," {he} says. "I can climb walls."
events.arc: The Matchmaker Who Will Not Give Up

choices.text: Help {npc} down from the roof

effects.log: {npc} takes your hand and slips the horoscope into your sleeve on the way down. It is an excellent horoscope.

choices.text: Leave town for a season

effects.log: You go up into the mountains. When you come down, {npc} is waiting at the foot of the path with tea and a new list.

choices.text: Hire a rival matchmaker as a distraction (10 taels)

effects.log: The rival lasts a week before the two of them go into business together. The list doubles.

events.text: Something has changed. {npc} comes to your door without a list, sits on the step, and admits that in forty years {he} has never failed a client, and never once been matched {him}self. Just once, {he} would like to know how it feels from the other side.
events.arc: The Matchmaker Who Will Not Give Up

choices.text: Offer to find {npc} a match

effects.log: {npc} stares at you, then laughs until {he} has to hold the doorframe. "Yes. Let us see how good you are."

choices.text: Agree to one real meeting, for {npc}

effects.log: {npc} puts the book away and pours the tea. "Then I will choose very carefully," {he} says. "This one is my last."

choices.text: Tell {npc} to go home

effects.log: {npc} goes, slowly. Next spring {he} is back with a list. Some people do not have it in them to stop.

events.text: Your career as a matchmaker is short and disastrous. Your first candidate for {npc}, a retired general, falls asleep at the table. Your second, a tea merchant, argues with {npc} about the price of tea for two hours. {npc} comes home from that one pink-cheeked and declares it a disaster.
events.arc: The Matchmaker Who Will Not Give Up

choices.text: Arrange a second meeting with the tea merchant

effects.log: Six months later {npc} marries the tea merchant, and seats you at the head table as the matchmaker. You have never been so proud.

choices.text: Admit you have no idea what you are doing

effects.log: "Nobody does," says {npc}. "That is the whole secret of the trade." {He} gives you the red fan.

events.text: {npc} brings the last candidate of {his} career to tea: a person of good humour and terrible handwriting. Then {he} sits at the next table the whole afternoon, pretending to read, mouthing advice.
events.arc: The Matchmaker Who Will Not Give Up

choices.text: Enjoy the afternoon honestly

effects.log: It is a good afternoon. Nothing comes of it but a friendship. {npc} counts it as a success, the last in the book.

choices.text: Wave {npc} over to join you

effects.log: The three of you talk until the lamps are lit. The candidate says afterwards that {npc} was the best part.

events.text: {npc} of the west market and Old Gong of the east market have loathed each other for thirty years, and both have decided to marry you off first. {npc} has come to warn you, in strict confidence, that Old Gong's candidates are frauds, spies and bad cooks.

choices.text: Become {npc}'s client

effects.log: {npc} is triumphant. By nightfall Old Gong has heard, and sends a candidate to your door at dawn out of spite.

choices.text: Become a client of both

effects.log: You sign with both. Neither knows. Both find out by noon. The war begins.

choices.text: Become a client of neither

effects.log: Both matchmakers take this as a challenge. You have made it much worse.

events.text: The war of the matchmakers is the talk of the district. Candidates queue at your gate from both markets. Today {npc}'s finest and Old Gong's finest arrive at the same moment, and must wait together on your bench, in silence, for an hour.

choices.text: Make them wait a little longer

effects.log: An hour becomes two. When you open the gate, the two candidates are deep in conversation and do not notice you.

choices.text: Meet them both over tea

effects.log: Tea for three. The two candidates keep agreeing with each other. You keep pouring.

choices.text: Send them both away

effects.log: Both go home together, sharing an umbrella. {npc} blames Old Gong's candidate for the rain.

events.text: Scandal: the two candidates from your bench have eloped, together, and written to thank you for the introduction. {npc} is outraged. Old Gong is outraged. Then, at your gate, the two old enemies look at each other and realise that a wedding is a wedding, and either of them could claim it.

choices.text: Suggest they split the fee

mem.note: made peace with Old Gong for me

effects.log: {npc} and Old Gong split the fee to the last copper, then argue in a teahouse over who made the match. They do it every week now.

choices.text: Claim the match yourself

effects.log: You claim the fee. The two matchmakers unite against you at once. For the first time in thirty years they are on the same side.

choices.text: Ask them both to find you nobody, ever

effects.log: They agree, solemnly. A week later, separately, each of them sends you a list.

events.text: {npc}, from the matchmaker's list, likes the same tea as you, the same sword forms, the same terrible street noodles and the same obscure poet nobody else has read. You both reached for the last dumpling at the same moment. It is too perfect. You suspect a trick.
events.arc: A Match That Is Actually Perfect

choices.text: Test {npc} with a trick question

ok.log: "That poem does not exist," says {npc}, and asks why you are testing {him}.

fail.log: The poem you made up turns out to exist. {npc} recites it, puzzled.

choices.text: Give {npc} the dumpling

effects.log: {npc} cuts it in half, exactly, and gives you the bigger half. It is unbearable.

choices.text: Ask the matchmaker how much {npc} was paid

effects.log: The matchmaker is offended. {npc} is amused. "Nobody paid me," {he} says. "I thought someone was paying you."

events.text: For your peace of mind, you hire a retired constable to look into {npc}. A month later the report comes back: no bribes, no scheme, no secret spouse, no rival sect. Only one dark secret: {npc} has hired a retired constable to look into you.
events.arc: A Match That Is Actually Perfect

choices.text: Laugh until you cry

effects.log: You both laugh until you cry, at the same moment, in the same way. It is still unbearable. You are starting not to mind.

choices.text: Demand to see {npc}'s report on you

ok.log: The report calls you "honest, stubborn and bad at hiding". You have it framed.

fail.log: {npc}'s constable was better than yours. The report is long. Some of it is about your snoring.

choices.text: Pay the constable to drop it (5 taels)

effects.log: The constable takes the silver and closes the case. {npc}'s constable, it turns out, was the same constable.

events.text: At last, a disagreement. {npc} believes a dumpling should be dipped in vinegar. You believe in soy. It is a bitter argument and lasts nearly an hour, and at the end of it you both feel enormously relieved that you are, after all, two different people.
events.arc: A Match That Is Actually Perfect

choices.text: Propose over the vinegar

effects.log: You propose with a dumpling dipped in both. {npc} says yes in the very words you were about to use. It is wonderful.

choices.text: Concede on the vinegar

effects.log: {npc} immediately switches to soy, out of courtesy. The argument begins again, backwards.

choices.text: Keep the argument going for years

effects.log: You agree to keep meeting until one of you gives in. Neither of you has the slightest intention of giving in.

events.text: {npc} comes to every meeting with a chaperone: an elder of {his} house, eighty years old, deaf in one ear when it suits, who sits between the two of you at every table with a walking stick across the knees. The elder has not yet spoken a word to you, and is said to frighten generals.

choices.text: Bow deeply to the elder

effects.log: The elder looks at you a long while and says nothing. {npc} whispers that this is a very good sign.

choices.text: Talk to the elder, not to {npc}

effects.log: An hour of weather, to an elder who seems to be asleep. {npc} says later that the elder heard every word.

choices.text: Pass {npc} a note behind the stick

ok.log: The note reaches {npc}. The elder's stick does not move, but one eyebrow does.

fail.log: The stick taps your wrist, gently, at exactly the right moment. The note is read aloud.

events.text: The elder sets three tests: a game of weiqi, a shot with a bow at a persimmon on a far branch, and a question, asked in a voice like an old door: "What do you do when {npc} is wrong?" You may choose one.

choices.text: Play the weiqi to win

ok.log: You win by half a point. The elder grunts and moves the stick a finger's width away from {npc}.

fail.log: You lose badly. The elder seems pleased you lost honestly, and teaches you the move.

choices.text: Shoot the persimmon

ok.log: The persimmon falls. The elder eats it slowly and offers you none.

fail.log: You miss the persimmon and hit the elder's hat on the gatepost. A terrible silence. Then a cackle.

choices.text: Answer the question

effects.log: "I say so, and then I wait to be told I am wrong too." The elder stares, then speaks to {npc} at last: "Keep this one."

events.text: At the next meeting the elder does not sit between you, but beside you, hands you the walking stick to hold, and spends the afternoon telling embarrassing stories about {npc} as a child. {npc} sits across the table with {his} face in {his} hands.

choices.text: Ask for more stories

effects.log: {npc} threatens to elope with somebody else. The elder says nobody else would have {him}.

choices.text: Ask the elder for {npc}'s hand

effects.log: The elder bangs the stick once on the floor, which in that house means yes. {npc} looks up, laughing. The wedding is in autumn.

choices.text: Defend {npc} against the stories

effects.log: The elder nods slowly. "Good. Somebody should."

events.text: By old custom a matchmaker brings a wild goose to seal a promising match. {npc} has brought you one early, on account. "For luck," {he} says. The goose bites {npc}, then you, then escapes over the wall, honking, with the red ribbon still around its neck.

choices.text: Chase the goose

ok.log: You chase it over three roofs. It lands in a courtyard in the next street and sits down on someone's washing.

fail.log: You fall off the second roof. The goose looks back once, with contempt, and lands in the next street.

choices.text: Let it go. It is a sign

effects.log: "A sign of what?" says {npc}, nursing a bitten hand. You both watch the goose land in the next street.

choices.text: Pay {npc} for the goose (3 taels)

effects.log: {npc} takes the silver and points at a roof in the next street. "Go and fetch it. I will wait."

events.text: The goose is sitting on clean washing in a small courtyard, and the owner of the washing, {npc}, is standing over it with a broom, deciding whom to be angry with. Then {npc} sees the red ribbon on the goose, and then you, and begins to laugh.

choices.text: Apologise for the goose

effects.log: "A matchmaker's goose," says {npc}. "Do you know what it means when one lands at your house?" You did not. You do now.

choices.text: Offer to wash everything again

effects.log: You wash the sheets at the well, badly. {npc} supervises with the broom, and gives you tea afterwards.

choices.text: Grab the goose and run

effects.log: You escape with the goose. Behind you {npc} shouts that you owe {him} a sheet.

events.text: {npc} has started turning up where you are: the market, the tea shop, the bridge. Always by accident. Always with the goose, which escaped from you the same night, moved into {his} courtyard and refuses to leave. The old matchmaker has given up asking for it back and calls it a sign.

choices.text: Admit you walk past on purpose

effects.log: "I know," says {npc}. "I count. Eleven times this month." The goose honks, very smug.

choices.text: Bring the goose a present

effects.log: You bring the goose a cabbage. {npc} says nobody has ever brought the goose anything. The goose bites you anyway.

choices.text: Stop walking past

effects.log: You stop. After a week the goose turns up at your door alone, ribbon and all. It is a hint.

events.text: The old matchmaker comes to {npc}'s courtyard with you, in best robes, and solemnly asks to take the goose back, for a wedding. The goose bites the matchmaker. {npc} looks at you, and the question hangs in the air.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to marry you

effects.log: {npc} says yes. The goose leads the wedding procession, bites two guests, and is the most honoured creature at the feast.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to wait a year

effects.log: {npc} agrees. The goose does not, and moves into your courtyard to keep an eye on you.

choices.text: Ask for the goose instead

effects.log: {npc} laughs so hard the goose takes offence. "The goose comes with me," {he} says. "Think about that."

events.text: {npc}'s letters are the most beautiful you have ever read: moonlight, rivers, a line about plum blossom that makes you sit down. They are also in three slightly different hands. Your own replies, it must be said, are written by a scholar for hire at the corner of the market.

choices.text: Keep paying the scholar (5 taels)

effects.log: The scholar's next letter for you is magnificent. {npc}'s reply is also magnificent. Something is not right.

choices.text: Write the next letter yourself

mem.note: wrote to me in your own hand

ok.log: Your letter is plain, short and true. {npc}'s reply is plainer and shorter, and in one hand.

mem.note: wrote to me in your own hand

fail.log: Your letter is plain, short and misspelled. {npc}'s reply is very kind about it.

choices.text: Pay the scholar a visit

effects.log: The scholar is evasive and has very inky fingers. On the desk lies a letter about plum blossom, in a hand you know.

events.text: The truth comes out in a teahouse. The scholar at the corner of the market has been writing both sides of the correspondence, for both of you, for two months, at double the price. {npc} turns red, then you do, then you both turn to look at the scholar, who has just come in for tea.

choices.text: Demand your silver back

effects.log: The scholar refunds half and argues it was the finest work of a long career. Neither of you can disagree.

choices.text: Laugh, and order three teas

effects.log: The scholar is relieved. {npc} asks which plum blossom line was the scholar's own. It was the best one.

choices.text: Ask {npc} which letters were really {his}

effects.log: "None," says {npc}, "but the river in the first one was my idea." It was the line you liked best.

events.text: Since the teahouse, you and {npc} write only in your own hands: bad grammar, crossed-out words, one drawing of a duck. The scholar at the corner of the market has heard, and offers, as a wedding present, to write nothing at all.

choices.text: Write a proposal yourself

effects.log: Your proposal is eleven words with one blot. {npc} writes back one word, in a hand you know at last. The scholar weeps at the wedding.

choices.text: Send {npc} a drawing of a duck

effects.log: {npc} sends back a better duck. It becomes a long correspondence of ducks.

choices.text: Hire the scholar once more, as a joke (5 taels)

effects.log: The scholar writes a parody of the old letters. {npc} laughs so hard {he} has to reply in person.

events.text: The matchmaker keeps a special list for people past forty-five, written in larger characters. Today's name is {npc}: widowed long ago, keeper of a medicine shop, and the elder of four grandchildren who arranged all of this behind {his} back and are now hiding in the shop next door.

choices.text: Make the grandchildren come and pour

effects.log: {npc} enjoys this enormously. Four guilty grandchildren file out and are made to pour the tea.

choices.text: Talk about the medicine shop

effects.log: You talk about roots and powders for two hours. You have not been so interested in anything for years.

choices.text: Admit you came to please the matchmaker

effects.log: "So did I," says {npc}. "Shall we enjoy the tea anyway?" You do.

events.text: You meet each spring and autumn. The grandchildren report everything to the matchmaker. Once, on a mountain path, your bad knee and {npc}'s bad back give out at the same moment, and you sit by the path for an hour, laughing, waiting for anyone at all to come by.

choices.text: Tell {npc} about your first love

mem.note: told me about the first love

effects.log: {npc} tells you about {his} own, long ago. Neither story is sad by the time the woodcutter comes.

choices.text: Carry {npc} down the mountain

ok.log: You carry {npc} down, slowly, both complaining about everything. It is the best walk of your year.

fail.log: Ten steps, and you sit down again. A woodcutter carries the two of you down, in turns.

choices.text: Share your knee medicine

effects.log: {npc} criticises your medicine, then improves it. Your knee has never been better.

events.text: The grandchildren have sent a formal letter through the matchmaker demanding to know your intentions. It is signed by all four and has a drawing of a wedding on the back. {npc} brings it to you, red-faced, and swears {he} had nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Answer the letter with a proposal

effects.log: You propose to {npc} before all four grandchildren, who cheer like a sect at a tournament. The wedding is small and very loud.

choices.text: Answer: a friendship for life

effects.log: You write that you will walk the mountain with {npc} every spring. The grandchildren are disappointed. {npc} is not.

choices.text: Ask the grandchildren for one more year

effects.log: {npc} laughs and says that at your age a year is a very bold promise.
